subject: Service surge attribution — SDK timeouts amplifying p99 regressions
messages:
From: Amy Lin <amy.lin@nova-retail.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes impacting checkout — urgent

Vivek,

We started seeing massive p95/p99 latency spikes on hosted API starting Tuesday evening (Mar 23) — checkout flows are timing out for a subset of requests and we have customers emailing in. Our telemetry shows a dramatic increase in error rates (502/504) and many of our frontends show client-side timeouts and retries. This looks like a Redwood regression on paper because the timings line up with your endpoint in traces, but we also saw an odd pattern: our SDKs automatically retry with short timeouts which seems to amplify traffic.

Attached is a small log bundle and a trace file (sdk_call_trace_amy.txt) showing repeated identical request ids being retried by our edge. Can we get an urgent investigation and a timeline? This is impacting the Pacific region and our post-holiday sale.

Thanks,
Amy Lin
Head of Platform
NovaRetail

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Amy Lin <amy.lin@nova-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Preliminary triage — p99 correlation with retry bursts

All — preliminary triage notes below. TL;DR: our backend saw a transient increase in concurrent in-flight requests starting 2027-03-23 21:10 UTC that aligns with NovaRetail traffic spikes. However, digging into request patterns shows a high volume of near-identical requests (same client request-id header) arriving within seconds — consistent with client SDKs doing synchronous retry loops with short timeouts.

What we observed:
- Grafana: p95 increased from ~120ms -> 450ms; p99 from ~320ms -> 1.8s during the surge window. Attached: grafana_p99_chart_mar24.png.
- Error mix: mostly 504 gateway timeouts and transient 502 on overloaded inference workers.
- Backend concurrency: single-model worker queues experienced bursts where queue depth hit 6x normal for short intervals.
- Trace samples (from the bundle): same request id retried 3–5 times within 12s windows. Retries are not exponential backoff — default client timeout appears to be 3s with immediate retry.

Hypothesis: client-side timeouts + aggressive immediate retries caused a feedback loop: retries added duplicate load to model workers which pushed latency into p99 region, which in turn caused more timeouts. When we see this pattern, the system looks like a server-side regression but the root cause is amplification at the client.

Immediate actions taken:
- Scoped a temporary rate-limiter on the NovaRetail API key (non-blocking, soft window) to prevent cascading failures while we investigate.
- Throttled routing for the busiest model pool to reduce queueing and stabilize p99.
- Captured additional traces and flagged for deep dive (INF-5123).

Next asks of NovaRetail:
1) Confirm SDK version and timeout/retry config. If possible, flip retries off for one tester and re-run failing flows.
2) Share any edge/proxy configs that could be reissuing requests.

I'll continue digging into kernel selection and queueing behavior but wanted to share this immediately.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: grafana_p99_chart_mar24.png (image), preliminary_traces.txt
From: Amy Lin <amy.lin@nova-retail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preliminary triage — p99 correlation with retry bursts

Thanks Sean — good detail and we appreciate the quick mitigation.

Quick answers:
- SDK: nova-edge-sdk v2.1.0 (we pinned it months ago). Default timeout in that release is 3s, retries are enabled with up to 4 immediate attempts (no jitter).
- Edge: our CDN/proxy doesn't retry at the HTTP layer, it's the SDK in our app code.

We've begun a staged test: disabling SDK retries for a small canary cluster and re-running checkout. Early signs: error rate dropped by ~60% for that canary and p99 measured from our edge improved. We'll share logs in a few hours.

Amy
Amy Lin
Head of Platform, NovaRetail

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Amy Lin <amy.lin@nova-retail.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Root cause and remediation plan — SDK timeout defaults causing amplification

Team / Amy — thanks for the collaboration and patience. Summary of the investigation and next steps:

Root cause summary:
- The p95/p99 regressions were triggered by a feedback loop where NovaRetail's SDK (v2.1.0) uses a 3s client timeout and immediate retry strategy. Under normal load this is fine; during a transient backend slowdown the SDK's retries produced bursts of duplicate requests that increased model worker queueing and caused backend latency to spike. The increased backend latency then caused additional clients to hit their short timeouts and retry, creating a spiral.

Why it looked like a Redwood regression:
- Traces showed the server experiencing higher concurrency and elevated queue times, so the visible interior metrics (p99) rose. Without correlating client retry patterns, this looks indistinguishable from a backend regression.

Immediate mitigations implemented by Redwood:
- Reduced request concurrency to the affected model pool by 30% for 48 hours to lower queue pressure.
- Enabled adaptive soft-throttles keyed by API key to cap retry amplification across all customers while we finalize mitigations.
- Filed INF-5123 for kernel/queueing improvements to better isolate short bursts.

Actions for NovaRetail (recommended, urgent):
1) Patch or configure nova-edge-sdk to increase default timeout to 30s with exponential backoff + jitter OR disable immediate retries for idempotent flows. We'll provide a recommended config snippet.
2) Apply client-side request-id header and make sure retries use the same idempotency token so we can detect duplicates server-side (we can add a quick guard in our routing).

Engineering follow-ups (Redwood):
- Short term: add detection for retry-amplification patterns (duplicate request-id bursts) to the Console alerts.
- Medium term: add a server-side duplicate-detection heuristic and graceful de-duplication for repeated request-ids within short windows.
- We will also publish a best-practice doc for SDK timeout/retry defaults and push a patch to our own official SDK integrations to recommend safer defaults.

Customer impact and next steps:
- NovaRetail: we recommend the SDK config change and to continue the canary; Redwood will keep the soft-throttle in place until traffic stabilizes.
- Exec brief: Vivek — I'll prepare a one-pager for your exec meeting and propose a small credit for NovaRetail for the operational impact.

Amy — please let us know when your canary is fully rolled back/updated and we'll remove the soft-throttle. We will coordinate a short postmortem and a joint customer-facing note.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Product Operations (Serving)
Redwood Inference
